label: Late copy phase: final step of length-3 sequences, or re-fed j
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase from recall_idx >= 2 onward. It never fires in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on the first two copy steps; it is active on about 2.3% of copy steps. The cleanest core is the last step of L=3 sequences (t=5, outputting orig(2) while orig(1) is fed back in): 96% precision there, holding 43% of activation mass, and it includes the top examples. The second component is the input token j being fed back late in the copy phase (rate ~10x baseline, ~31% of mass). Elsewhere the activations are weak and scattered over the last two copy steps (to_go<=1 holds 85% of mass) in short sequences (L=4) and at the final step of L=9, with other fed-back inputs such as r, l, o, g, n. Magnitude is largest in L=3 final steps with input j or o. The two-clause predicate reaches dev F1 0.44 and mass recall 0.72. Precision is limited because j fed back late in the copy phase often does not fire, especially in longer sequences.
